notes:
Borderline. Chinese-language primary accounts document government support, a collaborative network and frontier AI safety evaluation research. The network's own rendered site includes testing methods and audits in its research remit. These sources do not establish the government designation required by the tracker; they also do not prove that no designation exists. A standalone organisation, separate staff or budget, and already-published model tests are not status requirements. Older secondary descriptions saying the network has no model-testing function of its own are dated reports and do not exclude it now. Tsinghua dates its public debut to February 2025; this is not necessarily its constitution or designation date.

Tsinghua's Chinese account describes frontier-safety evaluation research and representation of China; its English account confirms CnAISDA organised the dialogue. The Zhejiang government-hosted speech reports government support for formation. No national designation act was identified. An essay by Zhao Yifan of the Xi Jinping Economic Thought Research Centre, first published in 科技中国 (2025, no. 7) and reposted on the NDRC website on 3 December 2025, recommends exploring government AI safety institutes. The repost identifies the original journal issue but gives no exact original publication date. This attributed commentary does not identify a commissioned study or review of the option, an appointed advisory inquiry, or an adopted government proposal. Its call for domestic AI safety institutes to join international cooperation does not name or designate such a body. The uncertainty is government designation, not whether a network can qualify or whether it has published evaluations.

Not a UN member; tracked as a territory. The AI Basic Act (passed 23 Dec 2025) requires the Ministry of Digital Affairs to provide AI evaluation and verification tools. AIEC is tracked as a related body because product testing alone does not meet the definition.

Chinese and English government accounts confirm AIEC's language-model evaluations, including Taiwan's language, social context and values. A 2024 ministerial transcript also discusses evaluating frontier models and working with international safety institutes. Separately, the National Institute of Cyber Security published DeepSeek jailbreak tests in February 2025 and AI-agent security tests in May 2026. The AIEC criteria concern trustworthiness and performance; NICS tests protection against attacks. Neither these activities nor the ministerial discussion alone establishes designation under route (a) or an ongoing qualifying public assignment under route (b). AIEC's methods site lists accuracy, reliability, fairness, privacy and security as its main evaluation items; security there means protecting the system against attack and misuse.

Resolution 0001/2025 Art. 19 prohibits requiring disclosure of source code, model architecture, weights or training data and bars mandatory third-party audits of these, and Art. 12(a) exempts providers of models, APIs and cloud services from mandatory registration on that basis alone; Art. 19 also limits ANIA to requesting high-level system descriptions, statistical summaries, performance metrics, dataset hashes and compliance statements. Legislative Decree 674 (Diario Oficial No. 178, 25 September 2026) sets special rules for carrying out national AI, robotics and similar technology projects; as read on 9 November 2026 it neither amends nor repeals Resolution 0001/2025.
